basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 36.' and it opens 'Vers. 36. Putiphari eunucho. Hunc alia translatio | non magistrum militiae, sed'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 36. Putiphari eunucho. Hunc alia translatio | non magistrum militiae, sed archimagirum. id est principem coquorum appellat, qui etiam sacerdos Heliopolis fuisse dicitur. Ubi quaeri potest quomodo uxorem habens sacerdos esse potuerit. Nam gerophantae Aegyptiorum non nisi casti et ab uxoribus alieni esse poterant. Tradunt Judaei Joseph pulcherrimum fuisse, et ob hoc ad turpe ministerium emptum, sed Deus ejus virilia arefecit, ne castum puerum corrumpere posset. Tunc factus est sacerdos Heliopolis, qui antea laicalis erat.
